Subject: Kickoff: model selection & token sizing for PraxisLegal

Hi Tessa,

Thanks for the intro from the sales team — excited to get this moving. A quick snapshot of what PraxisLegal is trying to do:
- Ingest large legal briefs and precedents (mostly PDF -> text) and expose a lawyer-facing assistant (short answers, summarization, clause extraction).
- Typical source doc: 4–30 pages; median 2,800 tokens, 95th percentile ~12k tokens after OCR/cleaning.
- Expected traffic: 200 active users during business hours, estimated 1,500 AI requests/day initially. Peak concurrency observed ~25 requests/minute during batched review sessions.
- Latency target: <600ms p95 for retrieval-augmented answers (RAG) where we only call a single generation model per request.
- Data constraints: US data residency, SOC2 required; NDA already in place.

We're looking for: a recommended model shortlist, context window sizing guidance, and a first-pass token volume estimate for budgeting. Can your CS/implementation team outline next steps and what you need from us?

Priya

Hi Priya — thanks for the details and the sample set. Looping in Ben (inference/runtime) and Mina (CS engineering) so we can align on the technical tradeoffs.

High-level plan from our side:
1) Quick sync (30–45m) to validate traffic shapes and confirm compliance constraints.
2) We'll produce: a) model shortlist by capability/cost; b) context-window recommendation and an operational token profile (concurrent/peak/day); c) a mutual action plan with milestones for implementation.

Preliminary asks for our prep:
- One or two representative documents (you included samples — perfect).
- Any SLAs you need beyond SOC2 (eg. uptime, incident response).
- Expected percent of queries that require full-doc context (vs. short snippets).

Preliminary shortlist (educated guess before we run evals):
- Option A (cost/mid-latency): 8k-window, high-quality open model (quantized) — good for single-pass answers with retrieved context.
- Option B (higher-cost/long-context): 32k-window LLM for full-document summarization and long-context clause extraction when you need entire brief in context.
- Option C (low-cost reranker + small generator): use a smaller generator with heavy retrieval and reranking for short answers at volume.

I'll schedule the sync for tomorrow and attach an initial token estimate workbook and a draft SLA for your review.

Thanks,
Tessa

Thanks — putting some rough numbers in the thread so Priya has visibility before the call. These are quick back-of-envelope estimates based on the doc sizes you shared.

Assumptions:
- Median doc after OCR: ~2.8k tokens
- 95th pct doc: ~12k tokens
- Users will tend to ask 1–2 questions per doc ingestion in early phases
- Retrieval returns ~3 chunks on average, each ~300–500 tokens

Scenarios (per-request token math, prompt+resp):
1) Short-answer (RAG, 3 chunks): prompt ~1,200 tokens (context + instruction) + output 150 tokens = ~1,350 tokens/request.
2) Summarize full brief (32k model): prompt ~8k tokens (extracted highlights) + output 500 tokens = ~8,500 tokens/request.
3) Clause extraction (long doc, chunked): 2 calls of scenario 1 (~2,700 tokens) or single long-context call (7–9k) depending on latency budget.

Volume estimate (initial month):
- Daily requests: 1,500 -> monthly ~45,000 requests
- If 80% are short-answer: 36k * 1,350 tokens = 48.6M model tokens
- If 20% are long/summary: 9k * 8,500 tokens = 76.5M model tokens
- Total monthly model tokens (gross): ~125M tokens

Operational notes:
- If you prioritize p95 latency, recommend pushing short-answer workload to an 8k-window quantized model with prefix caching and a small KV cache for common clauses. That reduces both latency and cost.
- For one-off full-brief summarization, we can route to a 32k endpoint with reserved capacity (can be scheduled during off-peak windows or billed as burst).

Action items for the call:
- Validate percent-splits (short vs. long) — Priya
- Confirm latency SLOs and acceptable trade for scheduled summaries — Priya
- We'll run a small eval suite (2–3 models) on your sample docs and share comparative cost/latency numbers within 48 hours.

-ben

Subject: PraxisLegal mutual action plan & next steps (model shortlist + sizing)

Hi Priya / Elena — great sync today, appreciate the clarity on percent-splits and budget. Below is the mutual action plan we agreed on and the immediate recommendations for model selection and token sizing.

Summary recommendations (finalized):
- Short-answer path (default): 8k-window quantized model (Option A). Rationale: meets p95 latency target at reserved capacity sizes we can keep within budget with aggressive prefix caching.
- Long-summary path: reserve a 32k-window model for scheduled summarizations. Route as a scheduled job or on-demand burst (higher cost).
- Fallback: small generator + reranker pattern for very high-throughput batch operations to minimize cost spikes.

Token sizing (based on agreed 85% short / 15% long split):
- Monthly requests: 45,000 (as discussed)
- Short-answer (85% -> 38,250 requests) * 1,350 tokens = ~51.7M tokens
- Long-summary (15% -> 6,750 requests) * 8,500 tokens = ~57.4M tokens
- Total monthly model tokens: ~109.1M tokens (gross)

Projected cost posture:
- With quantized 8k model + batching/caching: estimate fit within your $9k/month consumption target for the first phase (we will provide a concrete pricing sim in the workbook).

Mutual action plan (30-day onboarding sprint):
- Day 0–2: Redwood runs evals on your samples (Ben) and shares latency/cost table + recommended model image.
- Day 3–7: Implementation kickoff — instrument retrieval pipeline and prefix/KV cache patterns (Mina + Praxis engs).
- Day 8–14: Integrate monitoring and cost breakdown in Redwood Console; enable token-level traces and sample prompt captures.
- Day 15–21: Staged rollout: pilot group (10 power users), collect quality metrics and regression alerts.
- Day 22–30: Ramp to full initial cohort and finalize pricing commit or recommend Dedicated capacity if usage grows.

Action items assigned today:
- Priya: confirm any additional compliance docs (we have SOC2 + NDA; specify encryption/KMS needs).
- Praxis engs: provide a sample webhook for ingestion and one high-priority user flow to instrument.
- Ben: deliver the evaluation results and a sizing workbook by EOD +2 (you have token_profile_estimate.xlsx).
- Mina: will open a Console trial with token-level tracing and a shared dashboard link.

References and next artifacts we sent today: token_profile_estimate.xlsx; SLA_Draft_v1.pdf; PraxisLegal_MVP_prompt_set.csv. Links: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2bPraxisOnboard, HubSpot record: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/record/8237

If anything above looks off / you want changes to the sprint timeline, call it out and we'll adjust. Otherwise we'll treat this as the working plan and proceed.

Best,
